reason: E1 supports the use of a 5 nm ALD Al2O3 layer as a diffusion barrier for metals, but only up to 600 °C, which is far below the proposed 1100–1200 °C accident conditions. E2 supports the oxidation protection of Cr coatings on Zr-alloys at high temperatures and mentions Cr–Zr interdiffusion as significant, but provides no evidence for the Al2O3 barrier's effectiveness or stability at those temperatures. Thus, the critical premise that the barrier will function at 1100–1200 °C is unsupported.
premises: ALD Al2O3 layers can suppress metal interdiffusion at small scales
A ~5 nm ALD Al2O3 layer is a reliable diffusion barrier
ALD Al2O3 barriers are stable up to 600 °C
Cr coatings on Zr-alloys provide oxidation resistance at 1100–1200 °C in steam
Cr–Zr interdiffusion is a key failure mechanism for Cr coatings at high temperature
